'''Sir David Melville''', {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|CBE|FInstP|size=100%|sep=,}} (born 4 April 1944) is a British [[physicist]], academic, [[academic administrator]], and public servant. He was Vice-Chancellor of [[Middlesex University]] from 1991 to 1996, Chief executive of the [[Further Education Funding Council for England]] from 1996 to 2001, and Vice-Chancellor of the [[University of Kent]] from 2001 to 2007.<ref name="bio - Debrett's">{{cite web|title=David MELVILLE |url=http://www.debretts.com/people-of-today/profile/82046/David-MELVILLE |website=People of Today |publisher=Debrett's |accessdate=17 April 2016 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160513202111/http://www.debretts.com/people-of-today/profile/82046/David-MELVILLE |archivedate=13 May 2016 }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Melville was born on 4 April 1944 in [[Gateshead]], [[County Durham|Durham]], England.<ref name="bio - Debrett's" /><ref name="bio - FE Week">{{cite web|last1=Jones|first1=Rebecca|title=Sir David Melville: Rocket scientist who took on FE|url=http://feweek.co.uk/2015/11/09/rocket-scientist-who-took-on-fe/|website=FE Week|accessdate=11 August 2016|date=9 November 2015}}</ref> He was educated at [[Clitheroe Royal Grammar School]], then an all-boys [[grammar school]] in [[Clitheroe]], Lancashire.<ref name="bio - Debrett's" /> He studied [[physics]] at the [[University of Sheffield]], graduating with a Bachelor of Science (BSc) degree in 1965;<ref name="Sheffield DSc" /> he was the first of his family to attend university.<ref name="bio - FE Week" /> Having been awarded a [[NASA]] scholarship, he studied for a year at [[Columbia University]] in New York City, United States, and graduated with a [[graduate diploma]] in [[space physics]].<ref name="bio - Debrett's" /> During that year he worked on the [[Apollo program]]me of [[human spaceflight]] and the preparation of the [[Apollo 11]] [[Moon landing]].<ref name="bio - FE Week" /> He then returned to the University of Sheffield to undertake [[postgraduate research]] in physics. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degree in 1970.<ref name="Sheffield DSc" />

==Career==
From 1968 to 1984, Melville was a lecturer and then [[senior lecturer]] in physics at the [[University of Southampton]].<ref name="bio - LinkedIn">{{cite web|title=Sir David Melville|url=https://uk.linkedin.com/in/davidmelville|publisher=LinkedIn|accessdate=11 August 2016}}</ref> He then moved to [[Lancashire Polytechnic]] where he had been appointed Professor of Physics and head of its School of Physics and Astronomy.<ref name="bio - FE Week" /><ref name="bio - LinkedIn" /> From 1986 to 1991, he served as assistant director and then vice-rector of the polytechnic.<ref name="bio - LinkedIn" /><ref name="Kent DCL" />

In 1991, Melville moved to [[Middlesex Polytechnic]] having been appointed its director.<ref name="Kent DCL" /> He then oversaw its transition from a [[Polytechnic (United Kingdom)|polytechnic]] to a [[Universities in the United Kingdom|university]], and he became the first vice-chancellor of Middlesex University in 1992.<ref name="Kent DCL" /> During his time in charge, it expanded from 9,000 to 20,000 students.<ref name="Kent DCL" />

In 1996, Melville was appointed chief executive of the [[Further Education Funding Council for England]] (FEFC) in succession to [[William Stubbs (educator)|Sir William Stubbs]].<ref name="bio - Debrett's" /><ref name="THE - Marriages">{{cite news|title=Marriages made in heaven?|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/marriages-made-in-heaven/99709.article|accessdate=11 August 2016|work=Times Higher Education|date=2 August 1996}}</ref> As such, he was in charge of the £3&nbsp;billion yearly budget for [[further education]] and [[sixth form colleges]] in England.<ref name="Kent DCL" /> The FEFC was merged with the [[training and enterprise council]]s to form the [[Learning and Skills Council]] in 2001.<ref name="bio - FE Week" />

In 2001, with the closure of the FEFC, Melville returned to higher education as vice-chancellor of the [[University of Kent]].<ref name="Kent DCL" /> Over his six-year tenure at Kent, he oversaw the growth of the student population from 11,000 to 16,000 students.<ref name="Kent DCL" /> during this time he also served on a number of external bodies: he was chair of the [[Higher Education Statistics Agency]] from 2003 to 2007, chair of the [[University Vocational Awards Council]], chair of the Kent and Medway Learning and Skills Council from 2006 to 2008, and chair of [[Lifelong Learning UK]] from 2006 to 2010.<ref name="bio - LinkedIn" /> He left Kent in 2007.<ref name="bio - Debrett's" />

==Honours==
In the [[2001 New Year Honours]], Melville was appointed a [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) "for services to Education".<ref name="LG 30 December 2000">{{London Gazette |issue=56070 |date=30 December 2000 |pages=7–9  |supp=y }}</ref> In the [[2007 Queen's Birthday Honours]], he was appointed a [[Knight Bachelor]] "for services to Further and Higher Education", and was therefore granted the title ''sir''.<ref name="LG 16 June 2007">{{London Gazette |issue=58358 |date=16 June 2007 |page=1 |supp=y }}</ref>

In 1978, Melville was elected a [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics]] (FInstP).<ref name="bio - Debrett's" />

In 1997, Melville was awarded an [[Honorary degree|honorary]] [[Doctor of Science]] (Hon DSc) degree by the [[University of Sheffield]].<ref name="Sheffield DSc">{{cite web|title=Alumni|url=https://www.sheffield.ac.uk/polopoly_fs/1.87481!/file/YU3.pdf|publisher=Your University|accessdate=17 April 2016|page=35|date=2005–2006|archive-date=18 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170118101243/https://www.sheffield.ac.uk/polopoly_fs/1.87481!/file/YU3.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2000, he was awarded an honorary [[Doctor of the University]] (Hon DUniv) degree by the [[University of Derby]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Honorands|url=http://www.derby.ac.uk/about/organisation/honorary-awards/honorands/|publisher=University of Derby|accessdate=15 August 2016|year=2016}}</ref> In July 2008, he was awarded an honorary [[Doctor of Civil Law]] (Hon DCL) degree by the [[University of Kent]].<ref name="Kent DCL">{{cite web|title=Professor Sir David Melville CBE|url=http://www.kent.ac.uk/congregations/honorary-grads/archive/2008/davidmelville.html|website=Honorary Graduates|publisher=University of Kent|accessdate=17 April 2016|date=July 2008}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Melville is married to Hilary.<ref name="bio - FE Week" />
